title: Put a smartphone into its hybrid case the right way round and snap all four corners under the case's lip
keywords: phone case, smartphone, snap fit, camera cutout, press down, corner lip, everyday, bimanual
instruction: Put the phone in the case screen up, camera in the camera cutout, all four corners under the lip. Leave it on the mat.
context: About three in four smartphone owners keep their phone in a case, and putting a phone into a new or cleaned case is something most adults have done. A hybrid case (rigid clear back, soft rubbery bumper) has a raised lip that overlaps the screen edge all round, so the phone cannot simply be dropped in. Makers' instructions: line the top up with the camera cutout, get the top end in under the lip first, then press the bottom end down until its corners snap into place. Turned the other way, the camera block sits on the solid back, props that end up and it never seats; pressed in the middle or too lightly, a corner stays riding on the lip. The robot must turn a thin 171 g slab a quarter turn, set it on the case with its top end in, and press the corners straight down with a fingertip on the glass near the edge, firmly enough to push the lip back but on the glass, not on the lip.
setup: Metres from the midpoint between the arm bases (at (0, +0.305) and (0, -0.305)), x forward, y left, heights above the table top. Mat: grey felt desk mat 0.26 (x) x 0.50 (y) x 0.003, centred (0.18, 0.00), taped down. Case: Spigen Ultra Hybrid for Apple iPhone 15, Navy Blue (polycarbonate back, TPU bumper; listed 151.6 x 75.4 x 13 mm with camera guard, about 31 g), lying open, back down on the mat, centred (0.170, 0.000), long axis along y, its camera cutout at the left (+y) end on the far (+x) side. Pocket 148.0 x 72.0 mm, back 1.2 mm, bumper top 10.3 mm above the mat; its lip overhangs the screen edge by about 1.0 mm and stands about 1.3 mm above a seated screen (estimates from photos; README has the drawing). Camera cutout in the back: 32 x 32 mm, its centre 17.8 mm in from the +y inner end and 19.8 mm in from the far inner side. Phone: Apple iPhone 15 (147.6 x 71.6 x 7.80 mm, 171 g; aluminium frame, glass front and back), switched off, in no screen protector, lying screen up on the mat centred (0.170, -0.170), long axis along x, top end (earpiece, camera) pointing +x, away from the robot. Its camera block (about 28 x 28 mm, modelled 1.0 mm proud, estimate) is at the top-right of the back (seen from the screen side); with the phone the right way round in the case it sits over the cutout, i.e. the phone's top end goes to the case's +y end with the screen up. So the phone has to be turned a quarter turn (its top from +x to +y) and lifted onto the case. Gripper opening needed across the phone: 71.6 mm (limit 94 mm). Seating: the phone set on the case rests on the lip at both ends; each corner slips under the lip when pressed straight down on the glass near that corner with about 6-7 N (simulation; the real figure is an estimate, see fidelity). Nothing else is on the table. Both arms start at the ready pose, grippers open.
scoring: Judged once both grippers have let go (each gripper's centre point between the pads at least 30 mm from the phone's outline) and the phone and case have both been still for 1 s (moving under 0.5 mm and turning under 1 deg), from an overhead photo plus a caliper depth rod at each corner. Right way round: screen up (tilted under 10 deg from the case's back) and the phone's top end at the case's camera-cutout end (long axes within 10 deg), so the camera block is in the cutout. A corner is SEATED when, at that corner, the lip lies over the glass by at least 0.3 mm (photo/magnifier), the screen glass there is between 1.0 and 2.3 mm below the lip top beside it (depth rod: no higher than the lip's underside, and down in the pocket), and the corner is no more than 1 mm past the pocket's end or side wall. Score with the phone right way round: 1.0: all four corners seated, the case flat on the mat (tilted under 3 deg, resting on it) and its centre within 0.05 m of where it started. 0.75: three corners seated, or all four with the case moved or tipped. 0.5: two corners seated. 0.25: exactly one corner seated. 0.1: no corner seated but the phone resting on or in the case (its centre within 10 mm of the case's centre, its screen no more than 20 mm above the case's underside). 0.0: anything else, including turned end for end (camera block on the solid back), a phone still held or still moving, or lying on the mat. Sticky zeros (score 0 for the rest of the trial whatever happens after): the phone screen down at any time, the phone dropped (falling faster than 0.8 m/s, about a 33 mm fall), or the phone or case off the mat. Success = 1.0, held for 1 s.
run_limit: 2,400 steps (120 seconds at 20 Hz); the scripted demo reaches success at step 657 (plan 56 s)
reset_notes: Lift the phone out by pushing it up through the camera cutout and peeling the lip off one bottom corner, check the lip is not torn, and lay the phone screen up at its start pose with its top end pointing away from the robot. Set the empty case back at its start pose and wipe the glass. Nothing is consumed. Real trials use a non-working iPhone 15 display dummy ballasted to 171 g (see README, safety), rubber fingertip pads and an e-stop in reach.
fidelity: Phone and case are rigid. The TPU lip is modelled only where it snaps: four sprung end-wall sections, one per corner, 1.0 mm over the glass, each sliding back against a 1.5 N/mm spring (2 N preload) over a 45 deg lead-in, about 6-7 N straight down per corner; the real force is an estimate (no maker figure; see README). The long sides have a plain wall, no lip. Phone edges are bevelled, plan corners square. Lip size, camera block and cutout sizes are estimates from photos.
